quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn
No left turn
No U-turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. It has white background with red and black markings. It tells drivers that U-turns are not allowed here.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: The left portion
The center portion
The right portion

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This gives you a better view of the road ahead and helps other drivers see that you plan to move to the next lane.

questions.question: If your rear brake locks on a surface with good traction, what should you do?

options.text: Let go of the rear brake.
Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and only use the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop. On a surface with good traction, a locked rear wheel will not cause you to lose control as long as your motorcycle stays upright and travels straight.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
Only stop to yield to other traffic.
Vehicles will be entering the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, let all crossing traffic and pedestrians pass, then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: Is in the left part of a lane, next to the centerline.
Is in the right part of a lane, next to the curb.
Can vary depending on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can vary depending on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: The best lane position changes based on road and traffic conditions. Choose the position that gives you the best visibility and the most space around you. Move to different positions as traffic changes.

questions.question: What color are service signs?

options.text: Orange with black letters.
Blue with white letters.
Green with white letters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blue with white letters.
questions.explanation: Service signs are blue with white letters. They show where you can find rest areas, gas stations, food, hospitals, and other services.

questions.question: To turn safely on a motorcycle, you should always:

options.text: Lean in the direction of the curve.
Slow down in the turn.
Turn by using only the handle bars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean in the direction of the curve.
questions.explanation: Always lean in the direction of the turn. Slow down before you enter the turn, not during it.

questions.question: In which lane position are motorcyclists usually easiest to see?

options.text: The right
The center
The left

questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: The center lane position is usually best when following another vehicle. This position puts you in the driver's rearview mirror. Always be ready to change positions if traffic or conditions change.

questions.question: Before you start riding, make sure the fuel valve is:

options.text: Open.
Closed.
Covered.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open.
questions.explanation: Open the fuel valve before you ride. If it is closed, the engine may start with fuel left in the lines but will stop once that fuel runs out.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Move closer to the vehicle in front of you so you can use its lights to see farther down the road.
Keep riding at your normal speed to lower the risk of being struck from behind.
Reduce your speed and increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed and increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Slow down and stay farther behind other vehicles at night. It is harder to see in the dark, and you need more time and space to react to hazards.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Yield to other drivers.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.
Sit so your arms are straight when reaching for the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Your elbows should bend slightly when holding the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank to help you balance.

questions.question: The key to making a quick turn is to:

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Get your motorcycle to lean quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get your motorcycle to lean quickly.
questions.explanation: To make a sharp turn, your motorcycle must lean quickly in the direction you want to turn. The sharper the turn, the more lean you need.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle, you:

options.text: May exceed the speed limit by 10 mph.
Must not exceed the speed limit.
Are required to ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must not exceed the speed limit.
questions.explanation: Stay within the speed limit when passing. Only pass where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You have more time to react to the movements of other drivers.
You have space to maneuver.
You have limited escape route options.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have limited escape route options.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between you and other vehicles gives you time to react and room to maneuver safely. This is a benefit, not a problem.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger on your motorcycle, you should instruct the passenger to:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before the engine starts.
Sit as far back as possible on the bike.
Not talk or move unnecessarily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not talk or move unnecessarily.
questions.explanation: Tell passengers to avoid talking or moving while the motorcycle is moving. Passengers should get on only after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.

questions.question: If you get a flat tire while riding, you should:

options.text: Hold the handle grips firmly and stay off the brakes.
Shift your weight toward the good wheel and brake normally.
Brake on the good wheel while immediately pulling off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handle grips firmly and stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the handgrips firmly and stay on a straight course. Only brake if you know which tire is flat. Leave the road once you have slowed down.

questions.question: Part of your normal scanning routine while riding should include:

options.text: Constantly looking in the rearview mirror.
Frequent rearview mirror checks.
Not using the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Frequent rearview mirror checks.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror often as part of your normal riding routine. Also check your mirrors before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: When riding at night, maintain a minimum following distance of:

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge distances in the dark. Keep at least three seconds of space between your motorcycle and other vehicles when riding at night.

questions.question: Eye protection is:

options.text: Required for all riders.
Not required, but recommended.
Only required for inexperienced motorcycle users.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required for all riders.
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all motorcycle riders to wear eye protection while riding. A full face shield offers the best protection.

questions.question: A motorized scooter can:

options.text: Only be operated during the day.
Be operated without a driver license.
Be operated with any class of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be operated with any class of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, a motorized scooter can be operated by anyone who has any class of driver license.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride?

options.text: The left portion of the lane.
The center portion of the lane.
The right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. This is the safest position. Riding near the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding far from the passing vehicle may make the driver return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists pass another vehicle?

options.text: In a staggered formation
In pairs
One at a time

questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, motorcyclists should pass one at a time. Each rider must finish passing before the next one begins.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on a straight road:

options.text: You can usually maintain control of the motorcycle.
You will likely lose control of the motorcycle.
You will need to release the rear brake to regain control of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually maintain control of the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can usually control your motorcycle even with a locked rear wheel if it stays upright and goes straight.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead
Yield
Reduce speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is coming.
